First, we evaluate the inner integral by integrating with respect to $x$, treating $y$ as a constant:

$$
\begin{aligned}{\int }_{0}^{\pi /4}[{\int }_{\pi /2}^{3\pi /4}\frac{1}{{sin}^{2}⁡x{cos}^{2}⁡y}\,\text{d}x]\text{d}y & ={\int }_{0}^{\pi /4}\frac{1}{{cos}^{2}⁡y}[{\int }_{\pi /2}^{3\pi /4}\frac{1}{{sin}^{2}⁡x}\,\text{d}x]\text{d}y \\  & ={\int }_{0}^{\pi /4}\frac{1}{{cos}^{2}⁡y}[-\operatorname{cot}⁡x]_{\pi /2}^{3\pi /4}\,\text{d}y \\  & ={\int }_{0}^{\pi /4}\frac{1}{{cos}^{2}⁡y}(-\operatorname{cot}⁡\frac{3\pi }{4}+\operatorname{cot}⁡\frac{\pi }{2})\text{d}y \\  & ={\int }_{0}^{\pi /4}\frac{1}{{cos}^{2}⁡y}(-(-1)+0)\text{d}y \\  & ={\int }_{0}^{\pi /4}\frac{1}{{cos}^{2}⁡y}\,\text{d}y\end{aligned}
$$

Then, we integrate with respect to $y:$

$$
\begin{aligned}{\int }_{0}^{\pi /4}\frac{1}{{cos}^{2}⁡y}\,\text{d}y & ={\int }_{0}^{\pi /4}{sec}^{2}⁡y\,\text{d}y \\  & =[\operatorname{tan}⁡y]_{0}^{\pi /4} \\  & =\operatorname{tan}⁡\frac{\pi }{4}-\operatorname{tan}⁡0 \\  & =1-0 \\  & =1\end{aligned}
$$
